cards.title: Introduction to Directives
cards.content: Directives are special attributes with the v- prefix provided by Vue.js. They apply reactive behavior to the rendered DOM when the value of their expression changes.

cards.title: v-if vs v-show
cards.content:
v-if is 'real' conditional rendering because it ensures that event listeners and child components inside the conditional block are properly destroyed and re-created.

v-show is much simpler — the element is always rendered regardless of initial condition, with CSS-based toggle.

options.text: v-show completely removes the element from the DOM.
v-if toggles the display CSS property.
v-if conditionally renders or destroys an element based on a boolean expression.
v-show destroys child components on toggle.

cards.title: List Rendering with v-for
cards.content:
We can use the v-for directive to render a list of items based on an array. The syntax is item in items, where items is the source data array and item is an alias for the array element being iterated.

<li v-for="item in items" :key="item.id">{{ item.text }}</li>

content.template: To bind an attribute dynamically in Vue, we use the {blank} directive or its shorthand colon (:).

items.text: created (Hook called before the directive's bound element is mounted)
beforeMount (Called before the element is inserted to the DOM)
mounted (Called when the bound element's parent component is mounted)
unmounted (Called when the directive is removed from the element)
